issues.description: The solution implementation pushes printf arguments in the wrong order (push 123 then push hello) which contradicts the problem statement instruction to pass the format string first and then the arguments. The template uses the correct order (push hello then call printf). This mismatch between the problem statement and the solution can confuse students who inspect the solution to learn the correct calling convention for printf.
issues.suggestedFix: Modify the solution to push the format string (hello) before any argument values so the stack order matches the problem statement (push hello, then push argument values, then call printf), or remove the extraneous push of 123 if it is not needed. Ensure the solution's code and comments reflect the correct calling convention.

issues.description: The template uses a misspelled register identifier 'ecc' (add eax, ecc) while the problem statement and the solution use the correct register name 'ecx'. This typo causes a mismatch between the template and the expected/solution code and can confuse students about which CPU register is intended.
issues.suggestedFix: In helloWorld.asm (template), replace the incorrect identifier 'ecc' with the correct register name 'ecx' (change 'add eax, ecc' to 'add eax, ecx'). Optionally update the adjacent comment to reflect the corrected register name.
